subject: VPC delegation & operations playbook for attribution of network-related SLA impacts
messages:
From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helianthus.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Helianthus Ops <ops@helianthus.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delegation of network responsibility for private VPC deployment

Logan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we move toward the Private (VPC) deployment for Helianthus, Legal and Ops have asked for a concrete appendix that spells out how Redwood will attribute uptime/latency failures when some of the network stack is customer-managed. Specifically we need:

- A short "attribution matrix" showing which failure modes Redwood accepts responsibility for vs. ones that will be attributed to customer-managed networking (peers, NAT gateways, on-prem VPNs).
- The set of observability signals and endpoints Helianthus must expose (or allow Redwood access to) to support automated attribution (e.g., BGP session health, peering RTT measurements, egress NAT logs, KMS availability).
- A concise ops playbook for incident response during cross-boundary latency incidents — we want clear escalation steps, expected turnaround for remediation, and temporary fallback options.

Attached is our current VPC topology and a list of our peering addresses. We're proposing that any latency degradation measured between Helianthus-managed egress and Redwood's frontends over 60ms RTT or >2% packet loss be considered outside Redwood's uptime commitment unless Helianthus enables the requested telemetry and a jointly-agreed test harness.

Can Redwood produce a one-page attribution matrix + a short ops playbook we can review by next Wednesday (2026-09-22)? If so we can route the appendix into our procurement path and get Legal to sign a limited SLA appendix.

Jordan
CTO (interim)
Helianthus Health

Attachments: helians_vpc_topology.pdf (network diagram, 3 pages)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helianthus.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegation of network responsibility for private VPC deployment

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the diagram. We can produce the attribution matrix and a 2-page ops playbook. High level summary of what Redwood can and cannot own for Private VPC:

- Redwood responsibility (what we will commit to):
  - Inference runtime availability for traffic that reaches our ingress endpoints (TLS termination + model serving stack).
  - Token generation latency after request is accepted by Redwood (measured inside our environment).
  - Queueing/backpressure behavior and documented retry semantics.

- Customer responsibility (what we'd attribute to the customer):
  - Any intermediate network hop outside Redwood-managed peering or transit (including customer-managed NATs, on-prem VPNs, and third-party transit).
  - KMS availability for customer-managed keys when they are needed to decrypt payloads at customer side.
  - Traffic shaping or ACLs that introduce latency or drops on the customer side.

What we'll need from Helianthus to make this work:
- A short list of test IPs and a recommended RTT/packet-loss measurement method (we typically use a 10s ping+traceroute window plus TCP handshake time to our ingress).
- BGP session state or peering health telemetry (if available) or at minimum an eBGP health webhook we can query.
- Access to a short-term test harness (staging endpoints) so we can run a joint test.

Proposed technical attribution thresholds (draft):
- If path RTT (customer egress -> Redwood ingress) <= 40ms and packet loss < 1% -> Redwood accepts internal latency commitments (we will aim for 95th-percentile token latency X).
- If RTT between 40-100ms or packet loss 1-2% -> investigate jointly; Redwood may mark incident as shared and apply partial SLA credit after root-cause analysis.
- If RTT > 100ms or packet loss > 2% -> attribute to customer-managed network unless telemetry shows otherwise.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood drafts a one-page attribution matrix + a 2-page ops playbook and attaches a fillable "responsibility matrix" spreadsheet (vpc-responsibility-matrix.xlsx).
2) Helianthus provides test IPs and the staging harness by EOD Monday 9/20.
3) We run joint tests on 9/21; final appendix goes for signatures 9/22 if all good.

I'll attach the draft docs for your review. Priyom and Karthik are looped in for technical and procurement review.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-attribution-draft.pdf; vpc-responsibility-matrix.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Jordan Park <jordan.park@helianthus.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegation of network responsibility for private VPC deployment

Jordan / Logan —

Quick technical clarifications from infrastructure:
- The concrete threshold we can operationalize for attribution will be based on the 95th-percentile of observed RTTs over a 24-hour rolling window. For contract language we recommend: Redwood's availability commitment for the inference runtime applies when the 95th-percentile path RTT (measured from Helianthus egress to Redwood ingress using the agreed test harness) is <= 40ms and packet loss < 1% over the 24-hour window.
- Shared incidents: if the 95th-percentile RTT is between 40ms and 80ms we propose a joint RCA and a shared-credit model (percent credit to be negotiated; typical range 10-30%).
- For any KMS-integrated workflows using customer-managed keys, availability of the KMS is explicitly a customer responsibility; Redwood will document cached KMS behavior and fallback windows in the playbook.

Operational asks from Helianthus:
- Provide peering IPs, BGP neighbor identifiers, and the API/endpoint for any monitoring webhooks you can grant.
- Provide contact roster for on-call network engineer for 24/7 escalation (name, phone, pager).

I will update the draft appendix to show the exact metric language and include a sample shared-credit formula for joint incidents. If Helianthus can confirm the test IPs by Monday, we will be on schedule for the 9/21 joint test.

Karthik
Sr. Manager, Infrastructure Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@helianthus.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Helianthus Ops <ops@helianthus.ai>, Helianthus Legal <legal@helianthus.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegation of network responsibility for private VPC deployment

Logan / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the draft language. Helianthus accepts the proposed workflow and thresholds as the starting point for the appendix, with the following commitments from our side:

- We will provide peering IPs and a staging test harness by 2026-09-20 18:00 PT.
- We will give Redwood read-only access to BGP session health webhooks (details to follow) and the on-call contact for our network engineer.
- Helianthus Legal is prepared to sign a limited "Attribution Appendix" that will be attached to the main Master Services Agreement; please prepare a DocuSign-ready PDF.

Action items summary:
1) Redwood: finalize the one-page attribution matrix + 2-page ops playbook + fillable spreadsheet; provide DocuSign link by 9/22.
2) Helianthus: provide test IPs and webhooks by 9/20; legal will review the DocuSign envelope on receipt.

We will attach our internal signoff once Legal provides final counsel. Appreciate the pragmatic approach here — happy to run the joint test on 9/21.

Jordan
CTO (interim)
Helianthus Health

Attachments: signed-moa-draft.pdf
